title: Coral and the Oath
premise: Kestrel Almeida, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent their whole life in the valley of Hollowmere, where wards keep magic—and the dead—out. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars vanish from the sky, Kestrel learns they are the last heir of the Oathkeepers who once bound the realms together, and that the dead they hear are the murdered covenant-makers demanding restoration. Hunted by the Ashen Court, which feeds on the darkened sky and wants the covenant broken forever, Kestrel gathers a found family of exiles—a disgraced ward-smith, a starless astronomer, and a revenant knight—to reforge the covenant at the drowned altar of Coral. In the climax Kestrel must choose between silencing the dead forever (and keeping their own peace) or binding themselves as the living anchor of a new oath; they choose the oath, relight the stars, and return to Hollowmere no longer invisible but no longer alone.
about_author: Beatrix Almeida is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring funerary art before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, craft, and the families we build in the ruins of old promises.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Establishes Hollowmere's ward-quiet: no magic, no stars beyond the ridge, and Kestrel's secret—bone carvings that whisper with the dead. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking fear of being different.

chapters.title: Voices in Whalebone
chapters.summary: Kestrel carves a commission and hears a new voice: a woman naming names and dates of murders centuries old. First hint the dead are organized, not random. Beat: dread mixed with longing to be believed.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The sky over the valley goes black; the border wards shatter like glass. Magic floods in for the first time in living memory. Beat: terror and vertigo as the safe world ends in one night.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Hiding
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds the shattered wardstone bears their family crest. The Almeidas were Oathkeepers—the valley was a prison built around them. Beat: betrayal by one's own inheritance.

chapters.title: The Rider in Ash
chapters.summary: An emissary of the Ashen Court arrives, offering protection in exchange for Kestrel's blood, which can seal or break covenants. Kestrel refuses and flees. Beat: first refusal, first true danger.

chapters.title: Downriver, Against Sense
chapters.summary: Kestrel leaves the valley following the dead woman's directions toward the drowned altar of Coral. POV widens briefly to the Ashen Court hunting them. Beat: grief for home, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Ward-Smith of Brackish Ford
chapters.summary: Kestrel meets Odile Vane, a drunk exiled ward-smith who recognizes the crest and hates what Oathkeepers did to her order. She agrees to guide them—for spite. Beat: prickly alliance born of shared grievance.

chapters.title: A Market Without Sky
chapters.summary: In a trade city under permanent ash-dark, Kestrel sees how ordinary people survive without stars: sun-cults, hoarded light, fear of the dead walking. Beat: the world is bigger and crueler than the valley.

chapters.title: The Astronomer Who Counted Nothing
chapters.summary: Sef Ardent, a young astronomer whose life's work died when the stars did, deciphers Kestrel's bone-whispers as coordinates. Joins the quest. Beat: purpose reborn from loss.

chapters.title: Murder Most Covenantal
chapters.summary: The dead reveal how each covenant-maker was killed by the Ashen Court's founder—one of whom was an Almeida. Kestrel must reckon with ancestral guilt. Beat: shame as fuel.

chapters.title: Ash on the Road
chapters.summary: Ashen hunters ambush the group; Odile's improvised wards barely hold. Someone dies protecting Kestrel—a stranger who owed them nothing. Beat: the cost of being worth following.

chapters.title: The Revenant Knight
chapters.summary: They raise—or are raised by—Ser Ilex, a revenant bound to guard the road to Coral, who remembers the original oath firsthand. Beat: uncanny mentorship; the past literally walks.

chapters.title: Lessons in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Ilex trains Kestrel to speak with the dead deliberately rather than suffer their whispers. Kestrel learns the covenant's true terms. Beat: growing power, growing temptation.

chapters.title: The Court's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: POV shift: the Ashen Regent explains her philosophy—magic hoarded by the few starves the many; breaking the covenant was mercy. Her logic lands uncomfortably well. Beat: antagonist as mirror.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile admits she helped design the wards that imprisoned Kestrel's family, believing it contained a weapon, not a child. Rift in the group. Beat: trust broken and honestly earned back.

chapters.title: The Salt Marshes of Memory
chapters.summary: Crossing haunted marshland, Kestrel relives ancestors' memories through the dead—falling in love with a history that also horrifies them. Beat: empathy across centuries.

chapters.title: City of the Hoarded Light
chapters.summary: The party reaches Lumenhold, where the Court stores stolen starlight. Sef finds proof the stars aren't dead—only caged. Hope ignites. Beat: the quest gains a concrete prize.

chapters.title: A Theft of Small Brightness
chapters.summary: Heist chapter: stealing a shard of caged starlight. It works, barely, and the shard becomes their compass to Coral. Beat: triumph shadowed by how easily Kestrel enjoyed the deception.

chapters.title: Power Whispers Too
chapters.summary: The starlight shard begins speaking to Kestrel, promising they could silence every dead voice forever. Kestrel hides this from the others. Beat: corruption's first quiet hook.

chapters.title: The Turning of Ser Ilex
chapters.summary: Ilex's revenant bond frays; the Court offers him rest if he betrays Kestrel. He refuses—but the offer reveals the party is tracked. Beat: loyalty tested without betrayal delivered.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Drowned Altar Seen
chapters.summary: From a cliff, the party glimpses Coral: an altar-city sunk beneath a luminous sea, guarded by things that were once worshippers. Beat: awe and terror; the goal is real and monstrous.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Keep
chapters.summary: Quiet character chapter around a fire: each member names what they'd ask the dead for. Kestrel almost confesses about the shard—and doesn't. Beat: intimacy deepening the lie.

chapters.title: The Court Closes Its Hand
chapters.summary: The Regent takes Lumenhold fully, extinguishing the last free lights; refugees flood the roads. The party shelters them, becoming something like leaders. Beat: found family becomes found responsibility.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Sea
chapters.summary: With Odile's air-wards, the party dives to Coral's outer gates through gardens of bone-white coral grown from the old covenant-makers' remains. Beat: pilgrimage into the literal past.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Inside Coral, all the dead sing at once. Kestrel nearly drowns in their grief until Sef anchors them with a counted rhythm. Beat: vulnerability answered by love.

chapters.title: Terms of the Old Oath
chapters.summary: The dead lay out the covenant's price: a living anchor must hold it, feeling every realm's pain forever. The original Almeida fled this duty—hence the valley, hence everything. Beat: the family sin revealed as cowardice.

chapters.title: Refusal and Ruin
chapters.summary: Kestrel refuses the anchor role and tries a shortcut using the shard's promise to silence the dead instead. The ritual backfires, collapsing part of Coral and injuring Odile. Beat: hubris punished; lowest point begins.

chapters.title: Odile's Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's ward-scarred hands may never work again. She forgives Kestrel anyway, teaching them the final ward-work verbally. Beat: grace that shames more than anger could.

chapters.title: The Regent at the Gates
chapters.summary: The Ashen Court breaches Coral's gates—not to destroy the covenant but to seize the anchor role itself and rule both realms. Beat: stakes invert; the enemy wants the same door.

chapters.title: Sef's Star Charts
chapters.summary: Sef realizes the caged stars can be freed only while the covenant is being sworn—the two acts must happen simultaneously, in two places. The party must split. Beat: plan crystallizing from friendship's knowledge.

chapters.title: Ilex's Last March
chapters.summary: Ilex volunteers to hold the gate against the Court, buying time he cannot survive. His farewell reframes duty as gift, not chain. Beat: noble sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Shard's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alone briefly, Kestrel finally confronts the shard: it offers a painless eternity of silence. Kestrel breaks it, choosing to feel everything. Beat: the theme made flesh—power refused.

chapters.title: Climax I: The Gate of Coral
chapters.summary: Battle at the drowned gates. Ilex falls holding the line long enough for Kestrel to reach the altar. Beat: grief and fury fused into forward motion.

chapters.title: Climax II: The Swearing
chapters.summary: At the altar, Kestrel begins the oath as the Regent arrives to claim it herself. Their duel is fought in memory and voice as much as steel. Beat: identity versus ambition.

chapters.title: Climax III: The Anchor
chapters.summary: Kestrel accepts the full weight—every death, every realm's ache—and speaks the covenant whole. The stars ignite above the sea. The Regent, unanchored, crumbles to ash. Beat: transcendence through chosen burden.

chapters.title: Afterlight
chapters.summary: Dawn with real stars fading into morning. The survivors surface; the freed stars scatter home. Kestrel feels everything and is held by Odile and Sef. Beat: exhaustion, relief, tenderness.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: The realms begin negotiating the new covenant's terms—with Kestrel as anchor and witness, not ruler. Old orders must share power or dissolve. Beat: hope institutionalized, cautiously.

chapters.title: Burials and Beginnings
chapters.summary: The party buries Ilex at Coral's edge; the dead sing him properly home. Each survivor chooses a road. Beat: mourning that heals rather than hollows.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel returns to Hollowmere, now open to the sky, and frees the valley's records so no one is ever walled in again. Meets neighbors as themselves for the first time. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Coral and the Oath
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years later, Kestrel teaches young listeners to hear the dead kindly, with Odile and Sef beside them. The stars wheel overhead; the oath holds because it is shared. Final beat: power distributed is power uncorrupted.
